styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine: 21 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 25% neutral dark edges against 7% and 9%. The picture is weaker than the numbers. The grey-blue tile roof has only about 3-4 bands (a lighter top, a mid body and a dark base), with faint tile rows. It has none of the per-tile scallops or highlights that the Beodeul roofs show in 5-6 steps. The roof is also a wide, flat slab, and the references have a modelled hip or gable with a lit slope. The wall is a dark wood band with few grain dots. The awning stripes, the goods and the window are all clean and busy, but they are flat, uniformly outlined shapes with the sticker look. The outline is partly tinted, partly near-black along the roof and frame edges, so I call it mixed. Much of the tone count comes from the small, saturated goods and signage, not from shaded material ramps. Overall the building is rich in small detail but its main materials are shallower than the references. It would look flatter next to them.
